records.title: CSP concessions going to out-of-state operator
records.description: The South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks Commission meets tomorrow and plans to finalize a contract between Custer State Park and Xanterra Travel Collection, a move that commissioners said will help the park keep up with growing visitor expectations. Concessionaires are private companies that contract with the state to offer services that parks don’t provide, such as food, lodging and retail.

records.title: County has access concerns
records.description: Proposed access from planned multi-family housing on the property of the Bearded Buffalo Resort to Granite Heights Road has raised concerns from the Custer County Highway Department, Custer County Emergency Management and Custer County Sheriff’s Office.

records.title: Council breezes through light agenda
records.description: It was the quickest of meetings for the Custer City Council at its Oct. 5 meeting, as the council breezed through a short agenda in roughly 10 minutes. Among the agenda items addressed by the council was approval of the Custer Cemetery caretaker contract for 2027 with J&M Lawn Care. The terms of the contract call for the city to pay $49,500 for spring and fall clean up of pine needles, cones and branches, along with mowing and trimming the cemetery grounds. Noxious weed spraying as needed is also a part of the contract.

records.title: Meeting leads to senior board dismissal
records.description: In a 33-5 vote, members of the Custer Senior Center called for the dismissal of the current board of directors effective immediately at an unofficial emergency membership meeting Friday, Oct. 9. There is no established protocol for such a meeting in the Custer Senior Center bylaws. Tim Swanson was asked to run the meeting as the former board president, having willingly resigned Aug. 31.

records.title: Custer Chamber banquet Oct. 15
records.description: The Custer Area Chamber of Commerce’s 2026 Annual Chamber Membership Banquet will be held this Thursday, Oct. 15, at the Custer State Park Event Barn. Social hour begins at 5:30 p.m., followed by dinner at 6:30 p.m. and awards presentations. Several awards will be handed out to local businesses, citizens and organizations at the banquet. The awards to be handed out are: • Heart of Custer •Community Team/Service • Individual of the Year • Lifetime Achievement • New Business of the Year • Business of the Year • Custer’s Rising Star

Council discusses TIF funding for infrastructure
Several honored by Custer chamber
records.description: Some of Custer’s best were honored last Thursday evening in Custer State Park, as the annual Custer Area Chamber of Commerce Membership Banquet was held at the park’s event barn near the State Game Lodge. Among the awards presented was the Lifetime Achievement Award, which went to Phil Lampert, who presenter Amanda Carlin noted had shaped the Southern Black Hills like few others over a lifetime of work.

records.title: U.S. capitol tree stopping in Custer
records.description: The Custer Area Chamber of Commerce & Visitors Bureau invites residents and visitors to celebrate a special holiday occasion as the U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree makes a stop in Custer Tuesday, Nov. 10, as part of its journey from Idaho to Washington, D.C., where it will be displayed on the West Lawn of the U.S. Capitol.

records.title: State capitol rotunda restoration complete
Queen finally gives up jackpot
records.description: “I hope a local wins it.” That was a common refrain heard around Custer as the Custer VFW’s Queen of Hearts fundraiser reached its climax last Friday evening, as the jackpot swelled to $252,000 and people came from near and far to buy tickets for the chance to win just over a quarter of a million dollars. Some were said to have been spending thousands of dollars each week on tickets. Those who hoped someone local would win the prize got their wish.

records.title: Error on conservation district ballot
records.description: Custer County finance officer Dawn McLaughlin has announced the ballot for the upcoming General Election for the Conservation District Supervisor, Custer County race is in error. The race for election of conservation district supervisor states the following:  “You may vote for one or leave it blank.” The Custer County Conservation District Board of Supervisors has two open seats. Custer County received two valid petitions for the two open seats and those two candidates will be elected to fill the vacant seats without the necessity of an election.

'Watching bluebirds and fire' Oct. 27
records.description: JoAnn Stearns claims she has the best office view in the Midwest, and she’s probably right. For the last three years Stearns as been the lookout at Bear Mountain, which is one of six active fire towers in the Black Hills. It’s a great job with a rich history and she gets many interesting visitors every summer.

records.title: Get out and vote in General Election
records.description: Make sure you know what’s on the ballot before you vote in the 2026 General Election Tuesday, Nov. 3. From the top, U.S. Sen. Mike Rounds’ seat is up for a six-year term. Rounds, a Republican, is opposed by Independent candidate Brian L. Bengs. For U.S. Representative, Republican candidate Marty Jackley will face Democratic candidate Nicole “Nikki” Gronli for the two-year seat vacated by Dusty Johnson.

records.title: Merchants Trick-or-Treat Friday
records.description: The annual Merchants’ Trick-or-Treat is taking place in downtown Custer from 4-6 p.m. this Friday, Oct. 30. Community members are encouraged to dress up in their favorite costumes and enjoy a night full of trick-or-treating fun, treats, community and Halloween cheers.

records.title: City answers access questions
records.description: Custer County had questions. The City of Custer had answers. Questions and concerns raised at the Oct. 7 meeting of the Custer County Commission regarding access to Granite Heights Road for future residents planned multi-family housing at the Bearded Buffalo Resort were assuaged at the commission’s Oct. 21 meeting, as Trent Bruce of DGR Engineering, acting on behalf of the city, told commissioners of solutions and preparations already made for the housing.

records.title: Power transfers back to original board
records.description: After changing the locks three times in 10 days, the Custer Senior Center is back under the direction of the originally elected board members as of Oct. 19. This board includes Betty Sowder (president), Roberta Duncan, Tony Gonsor, Shirley Lake, Vickie Hanson and Al Krienke and will be referred to as board one for this story’s purposes. Another board was appointed by members of the Custer Senior Center at an unofficial emergency meeting Oct. 9 when members called for the dismissal of board one by a 33-5 vote. This group will be referred to as board two.

records.title: Housing project ready to launch
records.description: In order to attend the Homecoming Coronation ceremony Oct. 12, the Custer School District Board of Education moved its regularly scheduled meeting from Hermosa to Custer and breezed through a short agenda. The facilities and transportation committee met with the contractors who are going to be involved with the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Community Housing Project.

Veterans Day celebrations
records.description: Custer County is getting ready to honor veterans for their service with events Nov. 11 and 12. Starting in late October, Hometown Hero banners were hung on light poles around the City of Custer. The banners individually recognize veterans with photos in uniform and brief descriptions of their service.

records.title: County upgrades cybersecurity
records.description: Custer County is adding a new layer of cybersecurity to its technology infrastructure, all in the name of avoiding the kind of cyber attack that crippled Pennington County not long ago.

records.title: Project phases winding down for city
records.description: Progress was the theme of the Oct. 19 meeting of the Custer City Council, as the council OK’d a pair of notices of substantial completion of a pair of projects with the city, including West Dam.

records.title: Buffalo Auction is Saturday
records.description: The 61st Annual Custer State Park Fall Classic Bison Auction is scheduled for this Saturday, Nov. 7, at 10 a.m. When it rolls around, the park will be selling more animals than it has in recent years due to drought conditions.
